136.1: "When they were killed, the lord ofSunyaka became blind with fury. Heaving a deep sigh, he spoke thus to Kuti- laksa with his mind agitated on account ofhis eagerness for • war".
136.2: We have seven generals beginning with Balahaka. Send them to the battle-field as they have formidable power of arms.
136.3: The chiefs and the soldiers in the army consisting of thirty Aksauhinis followed them then, scraping the region of clouds through the numerous banners and flags.
136.4: Through the sounds (beatings) of the different war- drums such as Bherl, Nihsanas, Tampottas, Panavasand Anakas, they rendered the entire universe full of qualities of the Ether (viz. sound) at every step.
136.5: Taking the army consisting of thirty Aksauhinls, the extremely proud sons ofKTkasa started as though to enter Visva (the lord, i.e. to their death).
136.6: They were furious and hence they became red (in their face). Their armours were brightly illuminated by the suns' disc. Their weapons and ornaments glittered. Their hairs were tied up above heads. Thus the generals moved ahead.
136.7: They hastened to the battle ground waving weapons in their hands. With great fury they rushed towards the army ofSaktis.
136.8: With their loud shouts and shrieks they made the ten directions echo loudly. The proud Daityas (then) went to the place where the army ofgoddess was present.
136.9: A certain demon discharged ajavelin in the course of the battle. A certain Sakti cut off his javelin with an arrow. The same arrow killed him too.
136.10: A certain Sakti riding on an elephant trained her elephant in the art of butting against mounds, on the broad chest of a wicked Daitya.
136.11: A certain Sakti suddenly struck in its forehead the elephant on which a soldier of the enemy was seated. She struck it with a sword and gave it the pleasure of heaven (i.e. killed it.)
136.12: (Defective text) Another Sakti exterminated the enemies with sharp arrows and granted pleasure to her dagger in her own Romdli (A line of hair on the abdomen above the navel (i.e. the dagger was given rest).
136.13: With a blow ofher mace, certain Sakti smashed the chariot wheel ofher enemy and granted pleasure to her but- tocks with it (i.e. scratched it with it).
136.14: With her fierce sword a certain Sakti cut offthe pole, of the chariot ofa lordly Danava and enhanced the pleasure of the earth.
136.15: The army of Saktis infiltrated into the army of Daityas and the army of Daityas infiltrated into the army of Saktis.
136.16: The close intermingling of Saktis and the demons was like that ofwater and milk. During the time of fighting it confused both of them.
136.17: When the trunks and the tusks ofthe mad elephants of the Daityas were cut off by the swords of Saktis they appeared like huge boars.
136.18: Samharagupta the huge vulture of cruel eyes bore Balahaka who kept the bow well drawn in the course of the battle.
136.19: Seated on the back of vulture with his body moving up and down, Balahaka appeared like the Balahaka cloud (at the time of dissolution) clinging to a Kuta mountain with wings.
136.20: The leading Daitya, Suclmukha mounted on his vehicle crow. The root of its wings was as sharp (hard) as needle. Riding on this he fought a hard battle.
136.21: Then (the next general) Phalamukha took up a ploughshare as his weapon. Riding on a heron resembling a mountain, he shone brilliantly in the battle.
136.22: The leading Daitya named Vikarna, the extremely mighty general, rode on his vehicle the Bherunda bird and fought a fierce battle.
136.23: A fierce cock of extremely dreadful nature bore (the
136.24: Surveying the army of Saktis from the front with blazing eyes, and roaring loudly, the cock moved about mak- ing the hairs on its neck stand on their ends.
136.25: Thus, these seven evil-souled haughty Danavas, comparable to the seven oceans, harassed and tormented the soldiers of Saktis there.
136.26: Formerly, these seven Daityas had propitiated the sun-god by means of penance. Boon had been granted to them by the sun-god who had been pleased with their penance.
136.27: Looked at by them when eyes had been penetrated and occupied by the sungod, the innumerable weapons of Saktis became immobilized and they found their zeal (in war) futile.
136.28: When the missiles and weapons were blocked and immobilized by those seven sons of KIkasa, of great inherent strength, Saktis could not exert themselves.
136.29: Even when they exerted themselves they were over- come much by the immobilization of their weapons. So Saktis heaved a deep sigh and sat quiet.
136.30: Thereupon, finding a suitable opportunity, the Daityas who were directed by their masters, rose up with different kinds of weapons and smashed the army of Saktis.
136.31: Those Saktis who were deprived oftheir activity and who were prevented from using their weapons became perplexed and agitated on account of their arrows that could pierce even adamantine coats of mail.
136.32: The Saktis whose bodies had been wounded and pierced by the numerous weapons of Daityas in the battle field appeared like the creepers ofKarikola with plenty of good sprouts.
136.33: All those Saktis whose weapons were immobilized by them shrieked and wailed. Crying piteously, they resorted to goddess Lalita.
136.34: Then, at the bidding of the goddess, the deity Tiras- karanika (Magical veil), the body-guard of Dandanatha rose up in the arena oft he battle.
136.35: That Mahamaya (great deity of magical powers) got into an aerial chariot named Tamolipta with doors all round and assured Saktis about freedom from fear.
136.36: The Daityas were unable to bear the arrows that had the form and features of black serpents, that resembled iron clubs at their lower ends and that charged with the missile Mohana.
136.37: Thereafter, at the bidding of Dandanatha, the deity, Mother TiraskaranI discharged the great missile named Andha ( Blindingone) amidst the group ofenemies.
136.38: Their eyes were afflicted by the blinding arrows that were discharged from the bow Mahamohana of the goddess Tiraskaranika.
136.39: All those seven became blinded. They did not look at anything. In the absence of that vision, the immobilization of weapons came to an end.
136.40: Once again those (Saktis) raised weapons in their hands roaring like lions. With a desire to kill Daityas, they made preparations for the battle.
136.41: They kept the deity Tiraskaranika of great might in front of them. Due to the use of that good (effective) means, they became extremely delighted and fought.
136.42: "O Mother Tiraskarnika ofexalted fortune well done, "well done. You have appropriately screened off these wicked- souled enemies.
136.43: You are the great medicinal herb for screening (blinding) the eyes ofthe wicked. This troop of Daityas has been blinded by you.
136.44: O deity, this task ofthe Devas has been perfectly carried out by you since you have brought a disaster among these Daityas who cannot be conquered by us.
136.45: Hence, you alone, do kill these seven Daityas in the arena ofbattle. Raising up our weapons we shall destroy the entire army of these Daityas".
136.46: Oh being told thus and encouraged by those Saktis on account of their zeal for war (that deity Tiraskaranika) proceeded towards the army of Balahaka by means of the vehicle Tamolipta.
136.47: On seeing her advancing, those seven base Asuras immediately remembered the boon granted by the sun god.
136.48: Although the splendour ofthe sun entered their eyes, that destructive power within the eyes was overcome when the eyes had been covered by the prowess of Tiraskaranika.
136.49: The great asura Balahaka had formerly been blind due to his pride on being granted the boon as well as on account ofhis power ofweapons. He was blind due to anger also. Now he literally became blind on account of the missile (of the deity). Therefore, the deity Antardhidevata (i.e. Tiras- karanika) dragged him by his hairs and cut him off by means of Jier sword.

136.51: After cutting off his hardhead with a blow of her sharp-edged spear, she gradually killed the other five Daityas too.
136.52: The deity Antardhidevata made a garland with the seven severed heads of the Daityas by joining one another by means of their own tresses. Wearing that garland round her neck she roared loudly.
136.53: In the height of their fury, Saktis killed their army wholly and made many rivers of their blood flow.

141.2: I wish to hear about the exploits of SrldevI n the course of the battle. After seeing the mishap ofhis brother, w hat did Bhanda do, due to the grief thereof?

141.4: During the equinoctial periods as well as during the transits ofthe sun, on holy occasions and during the five Parvan* days, it bestows Siddhis ahd'glory. It destroys all sins.
141.5: On hearing that there in the battle his brothers had been killed. Bhanda was overwhelmed with great grief. He began to lament loudly.
141.6: With his hairs dishevelled and scattered, he fell on the ground in a swoon. He did not get any consolation. He became emaciated due to the sorrow for his brother.
141.7: Again and again he went on lamenting. On being pacified repeatedly by Kutilaksa, he got rid of his sorrow and became very furious.
141.8: The lord of Daityas who w'as a great chariot-fighter and haughty in war, mounted his excellent chariot called Abhila to which a thousand lions were yoked.
141.9: He hastened with great lustre like the fire of •world-destruction whose flames blazed. The name of his sword was Ghataka. It had the same shape as the Candrahasa sword.
141.10: When the armies moved here and there, dust columns were raised. Being unable to bear their burden, it appeared as though the earth went to the heaven.
141.11: Some ofthem who could not be contained on the earth moved ahead along the path of the sky. Some mighty warriors moved on riding on the shoulders of some.
141.12: Neither in the cordinal points nor on the sphere of the earth nor in the sky could they be contained. They moved on with very great difficulty as though they were addicted by the close contact of one another.
141.13: A loud roar resembling the rumbling sound of the cloud was given out by him who was moving on along with all the soldiers.
141.14: The universe became torn asunder by that exces- sively harsh leonine roar coming out ofthe mouth ofBhanda, the Daitya.
141.15: The oceans became dried up. The moon and the sun fled. The stars fell down from the sky. The earth began to heave to and fro.

142.2: On account of flawless and meritorious anecdotes of the goddess, I have become extremely delighted, O Haya- griva, The great power of MantrinI and Dandanatha also has been heard.
142.3: After the night of the fourth day of the battle had dawned, O Hayagriva, what did Ambika do after the battle was over?
142.4: Listen, O Pot-born Sage, O intelligent one, to what had been done by Jagadamba after Danava. Bhanda, had been killed.
142.5: With her eyes immersed in nectar (as it were), she repeatedly delighted the entire army of Saktis harassed and bruised by hundreds of weapons ofDaityas.
142.6: By the current of nectarine glances of the supreme goddess Lalita, saktis got rid of their fatigue due to her war. They became delighted in their minds.
142.7: In the meantime, Devas with Brahma and Visnu as their leaders, became gratified due to the smashing ofBhanda and they approached the goddess to serve her.

142.26: After assuming fresh forms and bodies. (or after making all our bodies fresh) by means of currents of abundant nectar of mercifulness, O beautiful deity worthy of being attained by cultured people *, the entire world has been resuscitated and rendered full of joy.
142.27: Thereafter, that evil-minded wicked fellow very haughty about his ability to fight in war, was killed by you. Now Kama has become Atanu (bodiless) for our sake. Hence you kindly do resuscitate Kama immediately.

142.29: By their union Kumara (Skanda), the leader of all the armies of Devas will be born. It is through that hero, alone that the king of demons named Taraka should be defeat- ed and driven away. 1
142.30: O deity with the designation Tripura, this helpless widow whose body has become very emaciated on account of the death of her husband takes refuge in you and bows down to you. Hence, please directa digit of your compassionate glance towards her".
142.31: After eulogising MahesanI thus, the excellent Devas beginning with Brahma showed her Rati who had become untidy and emaciated on account ofgrief.
142.32: That Rati who had abandoned all her ornaments on account of widowhood, whose face was covered with flow of tears, whose tresses had become scattered, and whose colour had become greyish on account of dust particles, bowed down to Jagadamba.
142.33: Gods wanted to kill Taraka for which Sankara must be tempted to marry. The pleading for Rati is in their own interest.
142.34: On knowing that both of them had their minds filled with devotion and that their inner souls had great bliss, the lotus-like face of the great queen beamed with smile. Look- ing at Rati who had kept her head bent down due to shyness, she spoke to Syamala thus: —
142.35: "O Syamala, let her take bath and let her be adorned with girdle and other ornaments. Let her wear gar- ments too as before, and then be brought here quickly".
142.36: "O mother Lalita, the physical body ofminc which had been burned by the eye oflsa has been restored to me due to the grace ofyour benign side-glance.
142.37: I am your son. I am your slave, employ me anywhere in any task".

142.39: These were the words of behest of Sri Lalita Devi. The cupid received the command of the goddess humbly and said "Let it be so". With palms joined in reverence, he set out from that place.
142.40: From all the hair-pores of the lord of Love arose many Madanas whose features were splendid and who could enchant the entire universe.
142.41: After fascinating and enchanting the entire sphere ofthe world through them, the cupid went once again to the hermitage of Sthanu with the desire to conquer the moon- crested lord.
142.42: He struck with his arrows, the moon-crested lord who was engaged in penance.
142.43: He frequently rolled in the flowery bed brought by the circle ofhis Ganas (attendants) the chief among whom were Nandin, Bhrrigi and Mahakala.
142.44: Supported by the hand of Nandin he went on from one flowery bed to another flowery bed and moved restlessly on it again and again.
142.45: Neither on the flowery bed nor in the nectar exuding from the crescent Moon nor in the snowy cold waters (of Ganga) did the heat offever of his body come down.
142.46: Tile Love-lorn condition of Siva like an ordinary person is described in W. 71-84. It is the author's special contribution not found in other Puranas.
142.47: On observing that this pain ofpassion could not be treated otherwise, Dhurjati exerted himself very much for the sake of marriage.
142.48: After enchanting the lord thus at the behest of Lalita, Kandarpa tormented the daughter of the lord of the mountain by means ofhis arrows. 1
142.49: Scorched and distressed by the fire of separation, Parvatl could not sleep at all. By the feverish distress of her body she enhanced the sorrow of her father.
142.50: On observing that his daughter's pangs ofseparation from Siva were irremediably severe, the lord of mountains felt great sorrow.
142.51: For securing her husband, Parvatl performed a very severe penance on the peak of the mountain Himalaya, named Gaurlsikhara.
142.52: She practised a dreadfully severe penance by stay- ing in water during the winter and by standing in the middle of fires with the eyes fixed on the sun during the summer.
142.53: Gratified by that penance Siva granted his proxi- mity to her. He accepted her as his wife in accordance with the religious injunctions regarding marriage ceremony.
142.54: Then after requesting for her hand through the seven sages at the outset, he married the lotus-eyed daughter, on being offered by the lord of the mountain.
142.55: Engaged in amorous dalliance with her for a long time, Mahesvara stayed in the abode ofhis father-in-law in the city of Osadhiprastha.
142.56: Thereafter, he came back to Kailasa along with all the Pramathas (attendants). He brought Parvatl there and thereby made the lord of the mountain (all the more) pleased.
142.57: Day by day, he grew up into a highly valorous hero. He was trained by his father and he acquired all lores.
142.58: On being permitted by his father he became the general ofthe army of the Devas. He killed Taraka along with Danavas.
142.59: Thereupon, he married Devasena offered by Sakra who was highly pleased when the leading Daitya Taraka was slain.
142.60: That glorious daughter ofSakra named Devasena became excessively delighted on securing Skanda as her husband.
142.61: After neatly accomplishing the task of Devas thus, the god oflove who enchanted the entire sphere of the universe went to Srlpura again.
142.62: There in the holy city ofSrlnagara' he went to that place, where Lalita ParamesvarT stayed for the sake ofthe pros- perity ofthe worlds. He went there in orderto serve her.

143.6: Again and again he went on lamenting. On being pacified repeatedly by Kutilaksa, he got rid of his sorrow and became very furious.

147.1: Henceforth, we shall recount different chambers of Vdpitraya (three tanks) etc. Merely by listening to these, great prosperity can be attained.
147.2: Within the thousand-columned enclosure and seven Yojanas away is the great chamber named Mandh. It is wonderfully built and beautified with all kinds of gems and jewels.
147.3: It has Gopuras. gateways, panels and bolts as before. The entire space within that chamber (enclosure) is a nectarine lake.
147.4: A series of steps in the lake are wonderfully paved with different kinds of gems and jewels. The swans and cranes in the lake are golden and gem-coloured.
147.5: The boat-women of Tara are crores in number. They are all in their fresh bloom of youth. They dance and repeated- ly sing the meritorious glory of the goddess.
147.6: Some of them have oars in their hands. Some have horns filled with water in their hands. They drink the nectarine water of that lake. They move about in hundreds of rafts and boats.
147.7: Rowing continuously in the waters of the lake, both clockwise and anticlockwise directions, Tar& guards this enclosure.
147.8: Within the enclosure of Manab&la (Chamber of mind) and seven Yojanas away from it is the enclosure well- known as Buddhti&la (Chamber of Intellect). It is four Yojanas in height.

148.10: Now I shall describe in detail the abode of Cintamani. Listen, O great sage. It is situated in the centre of Sripattana and it extends to two Yojanas.
148.11: Within the royal abode there are sparkling gemset lamps with their handle fixed on the walls. They have the splendour of ten million suns. They are fixed in various places all round, brightening the whole of the interior of the Mansion.
148.12: In the splendid central area of the mansion of Cinta- mani in a part of the altar is the great and lofty Hindu Cakra (Circular spot).
148.13: The space in between the lofty wall of the mansion of Cintamani and Birdu is after leaving off a KroSa occupied by the wall cited to be three Kro£as ( in width).

148.15: From Bindu to the PifheSa, there are fourteen different (sections). In the portion thus differentiated, the number of Hastas is being mentioned by me.
148.16: The interior of the mansion of Cintamani, 1 O Sage, is twenty Hastas above the level of the ground of the lotus grove. The Animd and other ( Siddhis ) abide there.
148.17: The extent of (the plot of the abodes of Aitimd etc. is four Nalvas. Four hundred Kifkus make one Naha, By the word Ki$ku it is a Hasta (cubit) that is mentioned.

148.25: They are considered to be fondled by the spontaneous flow of prose and poetry. They stay there, O Pot-born Sage, delighting and amusing Sri-Devi by means of sweet lyrics and dramas pleasing to the ears.
148.26: These divine weapons are extremely gratified by the blood of the wicked Danavas that was drunk by them in the course of the great battle with the Asura Bhanda. Those divine weapons are active and alert now.
148.27: Among other weapons there are supplementary weapons of these weapons. Their number runs into crores.
148.28: All those different kinds of deities remembered as pertaining to all the systems of philosophy serve the great goddesses there beginning wish Karnesi.
148.29: Sri Devi is the deity that completes the number when these deities as well as the deities named Nityas, Cakrinis and the Yoginis are reckoned. Mother Lalita who reclines on the lap of Lord Kamesvara is the fourth one in the group of Karnesi and others. She is the sixteenth among Nityas. 148.30: They are very close to Lalita, the consort of §rikame£vara. All their limbs are full with the freshness of youthful bloom and beauty. They are very attentive. They hold weapons.
148.31: Haughtily they move about both within the Bindu - pi (ha and all round too. They carry out the order of Lalita. They are the close companions and confidants of the VaJls.
148.32: All these have weapons with them. They are adorned with all ornaments. Above and below, they have the forms of pillars. They have personal forms in the middle.
148.33: They keep their eyes closed in meditation on Sri. Their limbs are steady without any movement due to medita- tion on Sri. Above them, the plank of the couch is Sad&£iva.

152.2: She employed Brahma in the task of creating the worlds, Vasudeva in the task of sustaining and the three-eyed lord (Siva) in the task of annihilation.
152.3: All these stay in Brahmaloka, Vaikuritha and Kailasa (respectively) always meditating on Mahalaksmi, the bestower of welfare.
152.4: Then the people in all the worlds abandoned the rites pertaining to the Devas and the manes. They were con- fused as to what they should do. They could not comprehend anything.
152.5: On seeing it, lord Rudra spoke to P&rvatl thus: — "Sin has been committed by you, O gentle lady, by closing my eyes.
152.6: The sages have abandoned their penances. The followers of the Vedic injunctions have dropped their Sandhya rites (Vedic prayers and rituals). O Ambika, all the Vedic rites have been ruined by you.
152.7: Hence, for the expiation of the sin, perforin the difficult task of penance. Go to Kail and perforin holy rites and observances there for some time.
152.8: Go to Kaflclpura afterwards. There you will see Kamakgi. Propitiate this eternal deity §iv& who destroys all sins.
152.9: Keep the Holy basil Tulasi plant in front of you, perform penance on the banks of Kampa".

152.11: "O dear ones, where had you been so long? Did you see Kamaksi seen by me? "
152.12: On hearing her words their eyes beamed with ecstatic delight. After placing the flowers intended for worship in front of her, they said: —
152.13: "It is true that the great goddess has been seen now by both of us. It is neither a dream nor an illusion. She directly went into your heart".
152.14: At the root of the sole mango tree, the lord (Siva) who was in agony due to separation from Bhavani, control- led his sense-organs and meditated on Kamaksi for the sake of acquiring Gauri.
152.15: Listen to another thing, O Pot-born Sage of great intellect. O sinless one, I shall tell you the power of the primor- dial Laksmi.

152.17: The skull of Brahma stuck to the nail of Bhairava who tried to shake it off again and again but it did not fall off.
152.18: In order to get rid of that sin of Brahmin-slaughter, he wandered over the whole of the Earth visiting all holy spots and the great rivers, like Gariga etc.
152.19: Kapali (one holding the skull i.e. Bhairava) was not released from that sin of Brahmin-slaughter. His very face indicated his despondent state. He appeared dejected and devoid of splendour. After a long time he reached Kafici where Brahma had stayed before.

152.23: On seeing that wonderfully excellent act of K&mak?i, the lotus-like face of Siva became delighted. He honoured it very much.

152.27: "O glorious one, I have spent a long time but I have not obtained a single son. My agony due to (yearning) for a son increases continuously. What shall I do whereby I will get a child? Please tell it to me."
152.28: The king duly honoured his preceptor who told him thus. Fbr the sake of obtaining a bosom-born son, the king duly presented to his preceptor various articles of gifts that he desired and sent him back.

152.32: For the purpose of subduing such sinful activities, go to the excellent city of Kaflcipura. After taking your bath hi the Kampa, see me the sanctifying (goddess installed there).
152.33: I am in the form of Mahalaksmi with only two arms. I hold a lotus (in the hand). I am CakreSvari, the great queen, invisible to ordinary persons with the gross (ordinary physical) eyes.

152.35: I shall be delighted and shall fulfil your boon".
152.36: Early in the morning the delighted king set out for Kaftcipura along with his wife, ministers and armies and reached it.
152.37: After meditating for a long time, the great king offered the deity many excellent garments and divine abodes. Thereafter, he eulogised her.
152.38: O goddess with the Pundra variety of sugar-cane shining as bow in the delicately soft and tender left hand, with the gem-set ring and flowery arrows beautifying the right hand.
152.39: O goddess who had conquered the beauty and splendour of the disc of the autumnal moon by the splendour of your face, whose cheeks have been adorned by the sparkling rays of gems in the earrings; O goddess who hold a lotus with an excellent fibrous stalk in the left hand, O Maheli (great goddess) with side-glances exuding a stream of kindness.
152.40: O goddess with conch-like neck sparkling with necklaces set with rubies and other jewels, O goddess having forelocks brightly illuminated by the crescent moon stationed on the forehead, O goddess having sparkling smiles and beautiful nose, O goddess who had conquered the petals of the blue lotus by the brightness of the eyes.
152.41: O goddess with excellent creeper-like eyebrows, beautiful face and remarkably fine forehead, O goddess who are like a female swan having its abode in the lotus of the Manasa lake of leading Yogins, O goddess having a large golden crown inlaid with gems and jewels, O goddess who are beautiful in every limb and who are worthy of being saluted by all leading gods.
152.42: O goddess who are the bestower of boons in accord- ance with the desires of the devotee, whose mind melts with compassion, who are proud (?) of her imperial assets, O goddess of the mystic wheel, O goddess whose lotus-like feet are served by Indra and other Devas, O great goddess of the throne, be manifest to me".
